elements.text: Topic: Advanced Variable Length Subnet Masks (VLSM)

segments.speech: Good morning, Roosevelt! Rise and shine, it's 6:28 AM and we are starting fresh today. With your exam on November 9th just 17 days away, we are diving straight into VLSM—Variable Length Subnet Masks. Let's get our minds sharp!

elements.text: Traditional subnetting wastes IP addresses by giving every subnet the same block size.

segments.speech: As a Management Information Systems student, resource optimization is everything. VLSM lets us slice a network into variable sizes based on exact host requirements, preventing massive IP waste.

elements.text: We allocate IP space starting from the largest required subnet down to the smallest.
Rule: Always sort host requirements descending!

segments.speech: To execute VLSM correctly, Roosevelt, the Golden Rule is to always sort your required subnets from the largest host count down to the smallest before allocating any addresses.

elements.text: Given network: 192.168.1.0/24. Requirements: Subnet A = 50 hosts, Subnet B = 25 hosts, Subnet C = 10 hosts.
Sorted Order: Subnet A (50) → Subnet B (25) → Subnet C (10)

segments.speech: Let's put this into practice, Roosevelt. Suppose we have the 192.168.1.0 slash 24 network and need subnets for 50, 25, and 10 hosts. We always allocate the largest requirement first!

elements.text: For 50 hosts, we need 2^h - 2 >= 50. The smallest block is 64 IPs (/26).

segments.speech: Let's calculate the first subnet, Subnet A, which needs 50 hosts. The closest power of two that gives us at least 50 usable hosts is 64, which is a slash 26 mask. Our range starts at 192.168.1.0 and ends at 192.168.1.63.

elements.text: ash of /26. This gives us 64 total IP addresses, with 62 usable hosts after accounting for the network and broadcast IDs.
Subnet A will therefore use the network range 192.168.1.0/26.
Next, we move on to Subnet B, which requires 25 hosts.

segments.speech: This gives us a slash 26, leaving 62 usable hosts for Subnet A. Next, we determine the requirements for Subnet B.
